title: Bicircular light tunable topological phases and nonlinear Hall responses in odd-parity magnets
abstract: Altermagnets are an emerging class of magnetic materials that exhibit characteristic features of both ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. Odd-wave magnets, where the momentum-dependent spin splitting follows an odd-parity form factor, provide a distinct platform for exploring unconventional magnetic and topological phenomena. In this work, we demonstrate light-induced topological phase transitions in odd-parity magnets driven by bicircular light. We show that a cascade of topological phase transitions occur as the relative amplitude ratio of the two beams is varied. These are accompanied by sharp changes of the quantum metric. We demonstrate that bicircular light unlocks nonlinear Hall responses arising from Berry curvature and quantum metric in irradiated odd-wave magnets, and formulate the underlying selection rules. Our results show that both the topology and the nonlinear responses in odd-parity magnets can be directly controlled by a bicircular drive.
summary: This work demonstrates how illuminating odd-parity magnets with bicircular light can induce controlled topological phase transitions. By analyzing the effective Hamiltonian via Floquet theory, the authors show that the light parameters can tune the Chern number. Furthermore, they establish that this driving mechanism generates and controls nonlinear Hall responses, providing a powerful tool for manipulating topological properties in magnetic materials.
main_problem: The study investigates light-induced topological phase transitions and the generation of nonlinear Hall responses in odd-parity magnets.
main_result: Bicircular light can directly control topological phase transitions, leading to tunable Chern numbers, and unlocks nonlinear Hall responses governed by specific selection rules.
method: The analysis employs Floquet theory and high-frequency expansions to derive effective Hamiltonians, followed by calculations of topological invariants and nonlinear response tensors.
model_or_system: The system models odd-parity $p$-wave and $f$-wave magnets, which are subjected to time-periodic driving from counter-rotating bicircular light.
key_observables: Chern number (C), quantum weight (K), Berry curvature dipole (BCD), and Berry connection polarizability (BCP).
important_parameters: Total light amplitude (R), relative amplitude ratio (r), and the frequency ratio (n) of the driving light.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the high-frequency expansion (Floquet-Magnus expansion) of the time-dependent Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the setup for light-driven topological transitions and nonlinear responses in a p-wave magnet. Figure 2 maps the topological phase diagram (Chern number and quantum weight) in the (R, r) plane.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the effective Hamiltonian under bicircular driving, determines the conditions for topological phase transitions via the Floquet mass, and then calculates the resulting nonlinear transport responses for both p-wave and f-wave models.
why_interesting: The explicit use of light-matter interaction (Floquet engineering) to control topological invariants and nonlinear transport in magnetic systems bridges quantum optics, condensed matter theory, and topological physics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of the illuminated odd-parity mag- net setup. Bicircular light drives topological phase transi- tions in odd-wave magnets and simultaneously enables tun- able nonlinear Hall responses. The counter-rotating Ω−nΩ bicircular light is shown illuminating a p-wave magnet as a representative.

FIG. 2. Chern number and quantum weight for the p-wave magnet under bicircular drive. (a) Topological phase diagram showing Chern number as a function of the total light amplitude R and the relative amplitude ratio r. (b) The quantum weight is presented in the same phase space. We ﬁnd that the quantum weight satisﬁes the geometric bound throughout the (R, r) parameter space, reaching large values near the phase boundaries. The other parameters are chosen to be n = 2, α = 0, t = 0.1, µ = −1.0, λ = 0.1, Jp = 0.3, θp = π/4, and Ω= 3.0.

FIG. 3. Nonlinear responses of the bicircular light driven p-wave magnet. Berry curvature dipole response for (a) r = 1.0 and (b) r = 1.5. The blue and orange curves show DΩ x and DΩ y , respectively. Berry connection polarizability response for (c) r = 1.0 and (d) r = 1.5. Here the blue and orange curves indicate χxyy and χyxx components, respectively. We note that the relative amplitude ratio of the bicircular drive, r, acts as a tuning knob for the nonlinear responses. We keep the remaining parameters ﬁxed at t = 0.1, λ = 0.1, Jp = 0.3, θp = π/4, α = π/4, n = 2, R = 2, and Ω= 3.0.

FIG. 4. Spin texture of the driven p-wave magnet. The expectation value of the z component of the spin is plotted across kx −ky for (a) r = 0.5 and (b) r = 2.0. The three columns show α = 0, π/4, and π/2, respectively. We ﬁnd that the spin texture can be tuned by the bicircular light parameters, in particular the relative amplitude ratio r and the relative phase α. Other parameters were chosen to be t = 1, µ = −0.250, λ = 0.3, Jp = 0.3, θp = π/4, Ω= 3.0, n = 3, and R = 2.

FIG. 5. Chern number phase diagram of bicircular light illuminated f-wave magnet. Bicircular light induces multiple topological phases characterized by C = ±1 and C = ±2. The phase boundaries are controlled by the total driving amplitude R and the relative amplitude ratio r. Here we set other parameters as n = 2, α = 0, t = 0.1, µ = −1.0, λ = 0.1, Jf = 0.3, and Ω= 3.0.
